2.3.m: the essence of grain, the milk of cows, the appearance of a water-jar in a well— / one should recognize this as a portent of the Sun; then one should make burnt offerings with lotuses.

2.3.s:
sahasraṃ juhuyādvātha tataḥ śāṃtirbhaveddhruvam ..
vikṛtāḥ pakṣiṇaścaiva pāṃḍukapotakāstataḥ .. 16 ..
2.3.d:
सहस्रं जुहुयाद्वाथ ततः शांतिर्भवेद्ध्रुवम् ॥
विकृताः पक्षिणश्चैव पांडुकपोतकास्ततः ॥ 16 ॥
2.3.m: Or one should offer a thousand; then pacification will certainly ensue. / Deformed birds, and then pale grey doves,

2.3.s:
śvetolūko bṛhaṃścaiva droṇakākaśca kokilaḥ ..
krauṃcaśca varddhanī caiva nipataṃti gṛhe yadi .. 17 ..
2.3.d:
श्वेतोलूको बृहंश्चैव द्रोणकाकश्च कोकिलः ॥
क्रौंचश्च वर्द्धनी चैव निपतंति गृहे यदि ॥ 17 ॥
2.3.m: a white owl, a large one, a raven, a cuckoo, / a heron, and a water-bird—if these descend upon a house,

2.3.s:
gṛhe tasya mahotpāto bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ..
sthūlabhaṅgapragrahaṇaṃ prarohaṇamathāpi vā .. 18 ..
2.3.d:
गृहे तस्य महोत्पातो भविष्यति न संशयः ॥
स्थूलभङ्गप्रग्रहणं प्ररोहणमथापि वा ॥ 18 ॥
2.3.m: a great portent will occur in that house, without a doubt; / the breaking of a large branch, seizing, or else sproutings,

2.3.s:
hārāḥ kaṭakaṭāyaṃte jātasya daṃtasambhavaḥ ..
hasatā devatānāṃ ca gātre svedaśca jāyate ..
sarpamaṇḍūkaprasavaḥ kuṃbhe vāpi kvacidbhavet .. 19 ..
2.3.d:
हाराः कटकटायंते जातस्य दंतसम्भवः ॥
हसता देवतानां च गात्रे स्वेदश्च जायते ॥
सर्पमण्डूकप्रसवः कुंभे वापि क्वचिद्भवेत् ॥ 19 ॥
2.3.m: necklaces rattling, the eruption of teeth in a newborn, / sweat arising on the body of laughing deities, / or the birth of serpents or frogs in a water-jar anywhere—

2.3.s:
nimittānyevamādīni jāyaṃte yasya veśmani ..
ṣaḍbhirmāsaiśca mriyate gṛhiṇī ca śubhā ca yā ..2.3.20.20..
2.3.d:
निमित्तान्येवमादीनि जायंते यस्य वेश्मनि ॥
षड्भिर्मासैश्च म्रियते गृहिणी च शुभा च या ॥2.3.20.20॥
2.3.m: in whose house such omens and the like arise, / within six months his good housewife dies.

2.3.s:
aśaniḥ patate yatra gṛhe vajraṃ ca pādape ..
śuklā vahnisphuliṃgāśca tasya viddhi mahadbhayam ..21..
2.3.d:
अशनिः पतते यत्र गृहे वज्रं च पादपे ॥
शुक्ला वह्निस्फुलिंगाश्च तस्य विद्धि महद्भयम् ॥21॥
2.3.m: Where lightning strikes upon a house or a thunderbolt upon a tree, / and white sparks of fire appear, know that great danger threatens him.

2.3.s:
kharjūra udarāvarte nikocagarale'pi ca ..
phalivṛkṣe tinduke ca yatra nirjāyate kvacit ..22..
2.3.d:
खर्जूर उदरावर्ते निकोचगरलेऽपि च ॥
फलिवृक्षे तिन्दुके च यत्र निर्जायते क्वचित् ॥22॥
2.3.m: Where on a date palm, udarāvarta, nikoca, garala, / fruit-bearing tree, or tinduka, it springs forth anywhere,

2.3.s:
udyāne devagehe ca svagṛhe caityavṛkṣake ..
kuryādādityavāre vā ayutaṃ tilapāyasam ..
tataḥ śāṃtirbhavedāśu dhenuṃ dadyācca dakṣiṇām .. 23 ..
2.3.d:
उद्याने देवगेहे च स्वगृहे चैत्यवृक्षके ॥
कुर्यादादित्यवारे वा अयुतं तिलपायसम् ॥
ततः शांतिर्भवेदाशु धेनुं दद्याच्च दक्षिणाम् ॥ 23 ॥
2.3.m: in a garden, a temple, one’s own house, or on a caitya tree, / one should offer ten thousand oblations of sesame milk-rice on a Sunday. / Then peace quickly ensues, and one should give a cow as a priestly gift.

2.3.s:
pāyasaṃ tilamudgau ca puṣpaṃ vā tālavṛntakam ..
ikṣumodakapiṇyākāñjuhuyādravimuddiśan .. 24 ..
2.3.d:
पायसं तिलमुद्गौ च पुष्पं वा तालवृन्तकम् ॥
इक्षुमोदकपिण्याकाञ्जुहुयाद्रविमुद्दिशन् ॥ 24 ॥
2.3.m: Milk-rice, sesame and mung bean, or flowers, palm leaves, / sugar-cane, modaka sweets, and oil-cake one should offer, intending the Sun.

2.3.s:
siṃhāsanaṃ rathacchatraṃ dhvajaścāmarabhūṣite ..
akasmāddṛśyate yatra rājño vānyatra kutracit .. 25 ..
2.3.d:
सिंहासनं रथच्छत्रं ध्वजश्चामरभूषिते ॥
अकस्माद्दृश्यते यत्र राज्ञो वान्यत्र कुत्रचित् ॥ 25 ॥
2.3.m: Where a throne, a chariot, a royal parasol, a banner decorated with chowries / are suddenly seen, whether belonging to a king or anywhere else,

2.3.s:
nadayaṃti ca satyasyojjvalanaṃ strīpuruṣayoḥ ..
āgamasya ca dṛṣṭvaiva bhaṃgaḥ kaṭakaṭāyanam .. 26 ..
2.3.d:
नदयंति च सत्यस्योज्ज्वलनं स्त्रीपुरुषयोः ॥
आगमस्य च दृष्ट्वैव भंगः कटकटायनम् ॥ 26 ॥
2.3.m: and they cause the blaze of truth to roar between a man and a woman, / and upon merely seeing their arrival there is breaking and rattling,

2.3.s:
upariṣṭādbhavedyasya mahotpāto bhavedayam ..
calatvaṃ cādharasyāpi tathā kaṭakaṭāyanam .. 27 ..
2.3.d:
उपरिष्टाद्भवेद्यस्य महोत्पातो भवेदयम् ॥
चलत्वं चाधरस्यापि तथा कटकटायनम् ॥ 27 ॥
2.3.m: or if it happens above anyone, this is a great portent; / and trembling of the lower lip as well as rattling [of teeth]—

2.3.s:
ruditaṃ kokilasyāpi ulūkopyaśubhaṃ vadet ..
rājāmātyavināśāya mahīṃ ca tatsuto'pi vā ..
hastino madayuktāśca mriyaṃte nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 28 ..
2.3.d:
रुदितं कोकिलस्यापि उलूकोप्यशुभं वदेत् ॥
राजामात्यविनाशाय महीं च तत्सुतोऽपि वा ॥
हस्तिनो मदयुक्ताश्च म्रियंते नात्र संशयः ॥ 28 ॥
2.3.m: crying of a cuckoo, or an owl screeching ill omen: / these lead to the destruction of the king and his ministers, or of his son on earth, / and elephants in rut die; of this there is no doubt.

2.3.s:
tāḍīpūgādayo yatra yamau syātāṃ pramādataḥ ..
gehī tatra vinaśyeta sadāraḥ putrasaṃyutaḥ .. 29 ..
2.3.d:
ताडीपूगादयो यत्र यमौ स्यातां प्रमादतः ॥
गेही तत्र विनश्येत सदारः पुत्रसंयुतः ॥ 29 ॥
2.3.m: Where palmyra, areca, or the like unnaturally bear twins, / the householder there will perish along with his wife and children.

2.3.s:
baddhapuṣpe yadā puṣpaṃ phalaṃ vā yadi dṛśyate ..
akṣatādarśanāttatra somasyādbhutadarśanam ..
dadhi madhu ghṛtaṃ caiva juhuyādayutaṃ dvijāḥ ..2.3.20.30..
2.3.d:
बद्धपुष्पे यदा पुष्पं फलं वा यदि दृश्यते ॥
अक्षतादर्शनात्तत्र सोमस्याद्भुतदर्शनम् ॥
दधि मधु घृतं चैव जुहुयादयुतं द्विजाः ॥2.3.20.30॥
2.3.m: When a blossom is seen on a flower-bud, or a fruit appears, / because of the disappearance of unhusked grain, that is a portentous sign of Soma. / O twice-born, one should offer ten thousand oblations of curds, honey, and ghee,

2.3.s:
pālāśaṃ somamuddiśya somasya ca bhaveddine ..
imaṃdevā iti maṃtreṇa somāya śrapayeccarum ..31..
2.3.d:
पालाशं सोममुद्दिश्य सोमस्य च भवेद्दिने ॥
इमंदेवा इति मंत्रेण सोमाय श्रपयेच्चरुम् ॥31॥
2.3.m: using palāśa wood, intended for Soma, on the day of Soma, / and with the mantra ‘imaṃ devāḥ’ one should cook a caru offering for Soma.

2.3.s:
utpataṃti gṛhe yasya yavā māṣāśca puṣkalāḥ ..
dadhikṣīrājyapākeṣu rudhiraṃ dṛśyate yadi ..32..
2.3.d:
उत्पतंति गृहे यस्य यवा माषाश्च पुष्कलाः ॥
दधिक्षीराज्यपाकेषु रुधिरं दृश्यते यदि ॥32॥
2.3.m: In whose house abundant barley and black gram fly up, / or if blood is seen in cooked curds, milk, and ghee;

2.3.s:
akasmādgṛhadāhastu anagnijvalanaṃ yathā ..
meghahīnā bhavedvidyudvṛṣasyodgamanaṃ tathā ..33..
2.3.d:
अकस्माद्गृहदाहस्तु अनग्निज्वलनं यथा ॥
मेघहीना भवेद्विद्युद्वृषस्योद्गमनं तथा ॥33॥
2.3.m: or a sudden burning of the house, like a blaze without fire, / lightning occurring without clouds, or the leaping up of a bull;

2.3.s:
vyādhilīnā vinaśyaṃti nikhilāḥ paśumānuṣāḥ ..
evaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni bhavaṃtyakārake dhruvam .. 34
2.3.d:
व्याधिलीना विनश्यंति निखिलाः पशुमानुषाः ॥
एवं सर्वाणि भूतानि भवंत्यकारके ध्रुवम् ॥ 34
2.3.m: all beasts and humans, overcome by disease, perish. / In this way all beings certainly suffer when Mars is malefic.

2.3.s:
rājāmātyavināśāya gehe gehī vinaśyati ..
prāṇanāśāya viprāyāhutyā ca prabhavaṃti hi .. 35 ..
2.3.d:
राजामात्यविनाशाय गेहे गेही विनश्यति ॥
प्राणनाशाय विप्रायाहुत्या च प्रभवंति हि ॥ 35 ॥
2.3.m: For the destruction of the king and his ministers, the master of the house perishes in his home; / indeed, through priestly oblations these portents bring destruction of life.

2.3.s:
dṛṣṭvā vābhadramatyugraṃ juhuyādayutaṃ kramāt ..
dadhimadhughṛtairyuktaṃ khādirodumbare'pi ca .. 36 ..
2.3.d:
दृष्ट्वा वाभद्रमत्युग्रं जुहुयादयुतं क्रमात् ॥
दधिमधुघृतैर्युक्तं खादिरोदुम्बरेऽपि च ॥ 36 ॥
2.3.m: Or having seen such very fierce inauspiciousness, one should duly offer ten thousand oblations / mixed with curds, honey, and ghee, into [wood of] khadira and udumbara,

2.3.s:
agnirmūddheṃti maṃtreṇa śrapitaṃ lohitaṃ carum ..
triviprānbhojayeddadyāddakṣiṇāṃ lohitaṃ tataḥ ..
svarṇamaṃgāramuddiśya tataḥ śāṃtiḥ prajāyate .. 37 ..
2.3.d:
अग्निर्मूद्धेंति मंत्रेण श्रपितं लोहितं चरुम् ॥
त्रिविप्रान्भोजयेद्दद्याद्दक्षिणां लोहितं ततः ॥
स्वर्णमंगारमुद्दिश्य ततः शांतिः प्रजायते ॥ 37 ॥
2.3.m: with a red caru offering cooked while reciting the mantra ‘agnirmūrdhā’. / One should feed three Brahmins, and then give a priestly gift of red cloth / and gold intended for Mars; then pacification arises.

2.3.s:
puṣpaṃ vā pātayedyatra phalaṃ vāpi tathaiva ca ..
dadhyannaṃ ca ghṛtairmiśraṃ raupyaṃ hiraṇyameva ca ..38..
2.3.d:
पुष्पं वा पातयेद्यत्र फलं वापि तथैव च ॥
दध्यन्नं च घृतैर्मिश्रं रौप्यं हिरण्यमेव च ॥38॥
2.3.m: Where a blossom or fruit drops down, / curd-rice mixed with ghee, silver, and gold,

2.3.s:
hastyaśvamahiṣā gāvo dārāpatyadhanāni ca ..
tuṣṭenāṃgārakeṇaiva sarvametatpradīyatām..
āṃgārakeṇa maṃtreṇa khādiraṃ cākṣatairyutam.. .. 39 ..
2.3.d:
हस्त्यश्वमहिषा गावो दारापत्यधनानि च ॥
तुष्टेनांगारकेणैव सर्वमेतत्प्रदीयताम्॥
आंगारकेण मंत्रेण खादिरं चाक्षतैर्युतम्॥ ॥ 39 ॥
2.3.m: elephants, horses, buffaloes, cows, wives, children, and riches— / all this should be given, with Mars being propitiated, / using the mantra for Mars, with khadira wood and unbroken grains;

2.3.s:
dakṣiṇāṃ ca yathāśakti dadyādviprāya vā punaḥ ..
lohitaṃ ca baliṃ dadyāttataḥ saṃpadyate śubham ..2.3.20.40..
2.3.d:
दक्षिणां च यथाशक्ति दद्याद्विप्राय वा पुनः ॥
लोहितं च बलिं दद्यात्ततः संपद्यते शुभम् ॥2.3.20.40॥
2.3.m: and again one should give a priestly gift according to one's means to a Brahmin. / One should also offer a red offering; then auspiciousness is obtained.

2.3.s:
dhāvaṃti cordhvapucchāśca gṛhe gāvaḥ svayaṃ yadi ..
ārohaṃti gṛhaṃ viprāḥ sārameyāśca sūkarāḥ.. 41 ..
2.3.d:
धावंति चोर्ध्वपुच्छाश्च गृहे गावः स्वयं यदि ॥
आरोहंति गृहं विप्राः सारमेयाश्च सूकराः॥ 41 ॥
2.3.m: If cows run of their own accord in the house with tails held high, / or, O Brahmins, dogs and pigs climb onto the house;

2.3.s:
gṛhe yasya bhavaṃtyete tasya bhāryā vinaśyati ..
sarveṣāṃ vā bhavenmṛtyurvaṃdhyā gaurvā prajāyate ..42..
2.3.d:
गृहे यस्य भवंत्येते तस्य भार्या विनश्यति ॥
सर्वेषां वा भवेन्मृत्युर्वंध्या गौर्वा प्रजायते ॥42॥
2.3.m: in whose house these occur, his wife perishes, / or death befalls everyone, or the cow becomes barren;

2.3.s:
mithyāvādena gehī ca rājñā vādaiśca tiṣṭhati ..
atha vā yadgṛhe gāvo nardayaṃti hasaṃti ca ..43..
2.3.d:
मिथ्यावादेन गेही च राज्ञा वादैश्च तिष्ठति ॥
अथ वा यद्गृहे गावो नर्दयंति हसंति च ॥43॥
2.3.m: and the householder faces false accusation and disputes with the king. / Or in whose house cows roar and laugh,

2.3.s:
dharaṇīhananaṃ yatra dvayorāskadanaṃ tathā ..
nimittānyevamādīni gośvajātāni sattamāḥ ..44..
2.3.d:
धरणीहननं यत्र द्वयोरास्कदनं तथा ॥
निमित्तान्येवमादीनि गोश्वजातानि सत्तमाः ॥44॥
2.3.m: where there is pawing of the earth, or the leaping together of two, / and such portents arise among cows and horses, O best of men;

2.3.s:
yasya gehe bhavaṃtyete nāśastasya bhaveddhruvam ..
maṇḍūkasarpakūṣmāṃḍāḥ prasuvaṃti yathā striyaḥ ..45..
2.3.d:
यस्य गेहे भवंत्येते नाशस्तस्य भवेद्ध्रुवम् ॥
मण्डूकसर्पकूष्मांडाः प्रसुवंति यथा स्त्रियः ॥45॥
2.3.m: in whose house these occur, his destruction is certain. / Just as women bringing forth frogs, snakes, and gourds—

2.3.s:
akasmādyadi caitāni budhasyotpātalakṣaṇam ..
śāṃtiṃ tatra pravakṣyāmi yathā saṃpadyate sukham .. 46 ..
2.3.d:
अकस्माद्यदि चैतानि बुधस्योत्पातलक्षणम् ॥
शांतिं तत्र प्रवक्ष्यामि यथा संपद्यते सुखम् ॥ 46 ॥
2.3.m: if these occur suddenly, it is a sign of a portent from Mercury. / I will explain the pacification there so that happiness may ensue:

2.3.s:
dadhimadhughṛtāktaṃ ca apāmārgaṃ tathā punaḥ ..
ayutaṃ budhavāre ca juhuyācchraddhayā yutaḥ .. 47 ..
2.3.d:
दधिमधुघृताक्तं च अपामार्गं तथा पुनः ॥
अयुतं बुधवारे च जुहुयाच्छ्रद्धया युतः ॥ 47 ॥
2.3.m: Anointed with curds, honey, and ghee, with apāmārga wood again, / one should offer ten thousand oblations on a Wednesday with deep faith;

2.3.s:
aṃbaketi ca maṃtreṇa budhāya śrapayeccarum ..
suvarṇaṃ budhamuddiśya gāṃ ca dadyātpayasvinīm .. 48 ..
2.3.d:
अंबकेति च मंत्रेण बुधाय श्रपयेच्चरुम् ॥
सुवर्णं बुधमुद्दिश्य गां च दद्यात्पयस्विनीम् ॥ 48 ॥
2.3.m: with the mantra ‘amba’ one should cook a caru offering for Mercury. / One should give gold intended for Mercury and a milch cow.

2.3.s:
suvarṇaṃ puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ ca suphalaṃ cākṣataṃ tathā ..
gṛhe prāṃgaṇake yasya nipataṃti kadācana ..49..
2.3.d:
सुवर्णं पुष्पवृष्टिं च सुफलं चाक्षतं तथा ॥
गृहे प्रांगणके यस्य निपतंति कदाचन ॥49॥
2.3.m: Gold, a rain of flowers, fine fruits, and unbroken grains, / if these ever fall into anyone's house or courtyard,

2.3.s:
alaṃkārayutāṃ vāpi sarvābharaṇabhūṣitām ..
gṛhamadhye tu yaḥ paśye tkṣīṇāmaṃtarhitāṃ striyam .. 2.3.20.50 ..
2.3.d:
अलंकारयुतां वापि सर्वाभरणभूषिताम् ॥
गृहमध्ये तु यः पश्ये त्क्षीणामंतर्हितां स्त्रियम् ॥ 2.3.20.50 ॥
2.3.m: or if one should see in the middle of the house an adorned woman, / adorned with all ornaments, wasted and then disappearing,

2.3.s:
akasmānmālatīpuṣpaṃ jātaṃ syāttasya vā gṛhe ..
somāya na ca saṃtuṣṭaḥ sarvametatpradṛśyate .. 51 ..
2.3.d:
अकस्मान्मालतीपुष्पं जातं स्यात्तस्य वा गृहे ॥
सोमाय न च संतुष्टः सर्वमेतत्प्रदृश्यते ॥ 51 ॥
2.3.m: or if mālatī flowers suddenly appear in his house— / not being pleased with Soma, all of this is seen.

2.3.s:
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ tathā putra aiśvaryaṃ ca varastriyaḥ ..
sabhṛtyāśca mahiṣyaśca mariṣyaṃti na saṃśayaḥ ..52..
2.3.d:
धनं धान्यं तथा पुत्र ऐश्वर्यं च वरस्त्रियः ॥
सभृत्याश्च महिष्यश्च मरिष्यंति न संशयः ॥52॥
2.3.m: Wealth, grain, children, power, and noble women, / along with servants and buffaloes, will surely die; of this there is no doubt.

2.3.s:
śrīścateti ca mantreṇa apāmārgaṃ tathā budhaḥ ..
sahasraṃ budhavāre ca juhuyād ghṛtasaṃyutam .. 53 ..
2.3.d:
श्रीश्चतेति च मन्त्रेण अपामार्गं तथा बुधः ॥
सहस्रं बुधवारे च जुहुयाद् घृतसंयुतम् ॥ 53 ॥
2.3.m: Reciting the mantra ‘śrīśca te’, the wise man should offer / a thousand oblations with apāmārga on a Wednesday, combined with ghee.

2.3.s:
payasvinīṃ tathā gāṃ ca vāsoyugasamanvitam ..
dvijāya śraddhayā dadyāttataḥ saṃpadyate śubham.. 54 ..
2.3.d:
पयस्विनीं तथा गां च वासोयुगसमन्वितम् ॥
द्विजाय श्रद्धया दद्यात्ततः संपद्यते शुभम्॥ 54 ॥
2.3.m: And a milch cow, along with a pair of garments, / one should give to a Brahmin with faith; then auspiciousness is obtained.

2.3.s:
raktasrāvo bhavedyatra tatra ṛtvikprasūyate ..
siṃhavyāghragavādīnāṃ dhanahānivipatkaraḥ .. 55 ..
2.3.d:
रक्तस्रावो भवेद्यत्र तत्र ऋत्विक्प्रसूयते ॥
सिंहव्याघ्रगवादीनां धनहानिविपत्करः ॥ 55 ॥
2.3.m: Where a flow of blood occurs, a sacrificial priest is born there; / among lions, tigers, cattle, and the like, it brings loss of wealth and misfortune.

2.3.s:
eko vṛṣastrayo gāvaḥ saptāṣṭa nava daṃtinaḥ ..
saṃvatsareṇa tasyaikā prasūtirvihatā punaḥ .. 56 ..
2.3.d:
एको वृषस्त्रयो गावः सप्ताष्ट नव दंतिनः ॥
संवत्सरेण तस्यैका प्रसूतिर्विहता पुनः ॥ 56 ॥
2.3.m: One bull, three cows, seven, eight, or nine tusked beasts— / within a year a single birth among them is destroyed again.

2.3.s:
punaḥpunarvrataṃ cāśu akāle maithunaṃ tathā ..
gāvo yatra prasūyaṃte yamau doṣakarāvimau .. 57 ..
2.3.d:
पुनःपुनर्व्रतं चाशु अकाले मैथुनं तथा ॥
गावो यत्र प्रसूयंते यमौ दोषकराविमौ ॥ 57 ॥
2.3.m: Repeated fasts immediately, copulation at improper times, / and where cows give birth to twins—these two produce harm.

2.3.s:
bhuñjīkṛtāni dhānyāni vrīhayo yavataṃḍulāḥ ..
grāvimārjāramaṃḍūkāḥ sthūṇābhaṃge ca prāṅgaṇe .. 58 ..
2.3.d:
भुञ्जीकृतानि धान्यानि व्रीहयो यवतंडुलाः ॥
ग्राविमार्जारमंडूकाः स्थूणाभंगे च प्राङ्गणे ॥ 58 ॥
2.3.m: Grains piled up together—paddy, barley, and rice grains— / stones, cats, frogs, and when a pillar breaks in the courtyard,

2.3.s:
vikiraṃti nakhairbhūmiṃ prarohaṃti grahaṃ tathā ..
gṛhe yasya prajāyaṃte tasyā mṛtyurna saṃśayaḥ .. 59 ..
2.3.d:
विकिरंति नखैर्भूमिं प्ररोहंति ग्रहं तथा ॥
गृहे यस्य प्रजायंते तस्या मृत्युर्न संशयः ॥ 59 ॥
2.3.m: if they scratch the ground with claws and shoot up in the house, / in whose house they occur, her death is certain; of this there is no doubt.

2.3.s:
ṣaṇmāsābhyantare yatra śmaśānaṃ yāsyati dhruvam ..
kalahaṃ jñātivairaṃ ca vyādhipīḍā bhaviṣyati .. 2.3.20.60 ..
2.3.d:
षण्मासाभ्यन्तरे यत्र श्मशानं यास्यति ध्रुवम् ॥
कलहं ज्ञातिवैरं च व्याधिपीडा भविष्यति ॥ 2.3.20.60 ॥
2.3.m: Within six months he will certainly go to the cremation ground; / there will be discord, hostility among relatives, and affliction from diseases;

2.3.s:
vipralāpo mitra nāśa iṣṭeṣvaniṣṭadarśanam..
bhāryāputravināśaśca bhavedeṣu viniścitam .. 61 ..
2.3.d:
विप्रलापो मित्र नाश इष्टेष्वनिष्टदर्शनम्॥
भार्यापुत्रविनाशश्च भवेदेषु विनिश्चितम् ॥ 61 ॥
2.3.m: delirium, loss of friends, sight of misfortune among loved ones, / and destruction of wife and son will certainly occur amidst these.

2.3.s:
kriyāvaṃtaṃ yadā kurvankurvīta gṛdhrabilvake ..
tadā rājñāṃ vibhramaśca tathā gṛhavināśanam .. 62 ..
2.3.d:
क्रियावंतं यदा कुर्वन्कुर्वीत गृध्रबिल्वके ॥
तदा राज्ञां विभ्रमश्च तथा गृहविनाशनम् ॥ 62 ॥
2.3.m: When performing rituals with a vulture on a bilva tree, / then confusion of kings and destruction of the house will occur.

2.3.s:
amātyavargāśca pure rājñāṃ rājyaparāṅmukhāḥ ..
bṛhaspatiṃ samuddiśya gāṃ ca dadyātpayasvinīm .. 63 ..
2.3.d:
अमात्यवर्गाश्च पुरे राज्ञां राज्यपराङ्मुखाः ॥
बृहस्पतिं समुद्दिश्य गां च दद्यात्पयस्विनीम् ॥ 63 ॥
2.3.m:
and the body of ministers in the city turns against the kings' sovereignty,
one should dedicate [it] to Bṛhaspati and give a milch cow.

2.3.s:
vārimaṃḍe ca kūpe ca vāpyāṃ ca madhukāṃjike ..
kṣīraṃ dadhighṛtaṃ caiva jātaṃ yadi bhaviṣyati .. 64 ..
2.3.d:
वारिमंडे च कूपे च वाप्यां च मधुकांजिके ॥
क्षीरं दधिघृतं चैव जातं यदि भविष्यति ॥ 64 ॥
2.3.m:
If in rice-gruel, a well, a reservoir, honey, or sour gruel,
milk, curd, and ghee should come to be produced,

2.3.s:
akasmāttatra vṛkṣaśca phalena saha saṃyutaḥ ..
gṛhamadhye prajāyeta tataḥ saṃpadyate śubham .. 65 ..
2.3.d:
अकस्मात्तत्र वृक्षश्च फलेन सह संयुतः ॥
गृहमध्ये प्रजायेत ततः संपद्यते शुभम् ॥ 65 ॥
2.3.m:
or if suddenly a tree laden with fruit
should spring up inside the house, then good fortune will ensue.

2.3.s:
bṛhaspatestu tuṣṭasya sarvametannidarśanam ..
gauraṃ bṛhaspateścaiva prakuryātprāyadakṣiṇām .. 66 ..
2.3.d:
बृहस्पतेस्तु तुष्टस्य सर्वमेतन्निदर्शनम् ॥
गौरं बृहस्पतेश्चैव प्रकुर्यात्प्रायदक्षिणाम् ॥ 66 ॥
2.3.m:
All this is a sign of Bṛhaspati being pleased.
One should make a predominantly white [gift] as sacrificial fee for Bṛhaspati.

2.3.s:
aśubhaṃ hi śubhenaiva śāṃtiṃ homaṃ ca kārayet ..
tatraiva rākṣasaṃ yatra ghaṭakaṃ pariśoṣaṇam .. 67 ..
2.3.d:
अशुभं हि शुभेनैव शांतिं होमं च कारयेत् ॥
तत्रैव राक्षसं यत्र घटकं परिशोषणम् ॥ 67 ॥
2.3.m:
One should avert inauspiciousness by auspiciousness alone, performing pacification and a fire offering
right where the pot, dried up by a rākṣasa, [is found].

2.3.s:
kesarī śarkarā tailaṃ rājataṃ tāṃḍavaṃ sthitam ..
māṣabhaktaṃ tathā dhānyaṃ suvarṇaṃ rajatāni ca .. 68 ..
2.3.d:
केसरी शर्करा तैलं राजतं तांडवं स्थितम् ॥
माषभक्तं तथा धान्यं सुवर्णं रजतानि च ॥ 68 ॥
2.3.m:
Saffron, sugar, oil, silver, dancing posture,
māṣa-rice, grain, gold, and silver pieces,

2.3.s:
tāmraṃ kāṃsyaṃ tathā lohaṃ sīsakaṃ pittalaṃ tathā ..
sthāpitānīva dṛśyaṃte gṛhe caitāni yasya vai .. 69 ..
2.3.d:
ताम्रं कांस्यं तथा लोहं सीसकं पित्तलं तथा ॥
स्थापितानीव दृश्यंते गृहे चैतानि यस्य वै ॥ 69 ॥
2.3.m:
copper, bell-metal, iron, lead, and brass—
in whose house these are seen as if placed [there],

2.3.s:
dhananāśo bhavettasya svarga bhaṃgo hyathāpi vā ..
vyādhipīḍe tathā ghore rājopadravabaṃdhane ..
gajāśvapaśubhṛtyānāṃ vināśo jāyate dhruvam .. 2.3.20.70 ..
2.3.d:
धननाशो भवेत्तस्य स्वर्ग भंगो ह्यथापि वा ॥
व्याधिपीडे तथा घोरे राजोपद्रवबंधने ॥
गजाश्वपशुभृत्यानां विनाशो जायते ध्रुवम् ॥ 2.3.20.70 ॥

2.3.s:
yasyaitāni pradṛśyaṃte parvataḥ kanakāni ca ..
saṃpattasya prajāyeta niścalā sukhadā sadā .. 71 ..
2.3.d:
यस्यैतानि प्रदृश्यंते पर्वतः कनकानि च ॥
संपत्तस्य प्रजायेत निश्चला सुखदा सदा ॥ 71 ॥
2.3.m:
For him to whom these, a mountain, and pieces of gold appear,
steadfast prosperity bringing constant joy will be born.

2.3.s:
daṃtottareṣu daṃtāśca paṃktimākramya saṃsthitāḥ ..
te'pi doṣakarāḥ sarve śalā kākṛtinastathā ..
upadaṃtāśca sarve te na te doṣakarāḥ kvacit .. 72 ..
2.3.d:
दंतोत्तरेषु दंताश्च पंक्तिमाक्रम्य संस्थिताः ॥
तेऽपि दोषकराः सर्वे शला काकृतिनस्तथा ॥
उपदंताश्च सर्वे ते न ते दोषकराः क्वचित् ॥ 72 ॥

2.3.s:
bhāṃḍe kuṃbhe yadā caiva śrūyate ghanagarjitam ..
kaṃcukānāṃ gṛhe caiva prākāraḥ śrūyate yadi .. 73 ..
2.3.d:
भांडे कुंभे यदा चैव श्रूयते घनगर्जितम् ॥
कंचुकानां गृहे चैव प्राकारः श्रूयते यदि ॥ 73 ॥
2.3.m:
When the roar of a dense cloud is heard in a vessel or jar,
or if the [shaking of a] rampart is heard in a house of mail-clad guards,

2.3.s:
mūṣikānāṃ mukhe caiva jvalaṃtī yasya paśyati ..
gehī tatraiva naśyeta śukrasyādbhutadarśanam ..74..
2.3.d:
मूषिकानां मुखे चैव ज्वलंती यस्य पश्यति ॥
गेही तत्रैव नश्येत शुक्रस्याद्भुतदर्शनम् ॥74॥
2.3.m:
or in whose house a blazing [light] is seen in the mouth of mice,
the householder there will perish: this is a portent of Śukra.

2.3.s:
śāṃtiṃ tatra pravakṣyāmi yayā saṃpadyate śubham ..
śamīpatraṃ nirmitaṃ ca yavairyuktaṃ gṛhiṇyapi ..
dadhimadhughṛtāktaṃ ca juhuyādbhārgave dine .. 75 ..
2.3.d:
शांतिं तत्र प्रवक्ष्यामि यया संपद्यते शुभम् ॥
शमीपत्रं निर्मितं च यवैर्युक्तं गृहिण्यपि ॥
दधिमधुघृताक्तं च जुहुयाद्भार्गवे दिने ॥ 75 ॥
2.3.m:
I shall declare the pacification rite for that, by which good fortune ensues:
the housewife should offer into the fire śamī-leaves prepared
and mixed with barley, smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, on a Friday.

2.3.s:
śuklavāsoyugaṃ caiva gāṃ ca śuklāṃ payasvinīm ..
suvarṇaṃ śraddhayā caiva dadyādviprāya dakṣiṇām .. 76 ..
2.3.d:
शुक्लवासोयुगं चैव गां च शुक्लां पयस्विनीम् ॥
सुवर्णं श्रद्धया चैव दद्याद्विप्राय दक्षिणाम् ॥ 76 ॥
2.3.m:
And one should faithfully give to a Brahmin, as a sacrificial fee,
a pair of white garments, a white milch cow, and gold.

2.3.s:
devāgāre yadā bhūmirlohitā yasya dṛśyate ..
puṣpitā dṛśyate loke tatra viddhi mahadbhayam .. 77 ..
2.3.d:
देवागारे यदा भूमिर्लोहिता यस्य दृश्यते ॥
पुष्पिता दृश्यते लोके तत्र विद्धि महद्भयम् ॥ 77 ॥
2.3.m:
When the earth in a temple is seen by someone to be red,
[or] is seen flowering in the world, know that there is great danger there.

2.3.s:
rājā vā rājaputro vā rājyaṃ vāpi vinaśyati ..
maṃtriṇo maṃtriputrāśca mriyaṃte nātra saṃśayaḥ ..78..
2.3.d:
राजा वा राजपुत्रो वा राज्यं वापि विनश्यति ॥
मंत्रिणो मंत्रिपुत्राश्च म्रियंते नात्र संशयः ॥78॥
2.3.m:
The king or the king's son or the kingdom itself will perish;
the ministers and the ministers' sons will die—there is no doubt of this.

2.3.s:
yatra vā dṛśyate loke gṛhe yasya supūjitāḥ ..
puṣpitāśca gṛhastaṃbhāḥ śarīraṃ ca ghaṭastathā .. 79 ..
2.3.d:
यत्र वा दृश्यते लोके गृहे यस्य सुपूजिताः ॥
पुष्पिताश्च गृहस्तंभाः शरीरं च घटस्तथा ॥ 79 ॥
2.3.m:
Or where, well-honoured in someone's house, there are seen in the world
flowering house-pillars, or a body, or a pot,

2.3.s:
hastyaśvamahiṣāścaiva ajā gāvastathaiva ca ..
nityaṃ svāmivadhārthāya puṣpitāṃ pravahaṃti ca .. 2.3.20.80 ..
2.3.d:
हस्त्यश्वमहिषाश्चैव अजा गावस्तथैव च ॥
नित्यं स्वामिवधार्थाय पुष्पितां प्रवहंति च ॥ 2.3.20.80 ॥
2.3.m:
elephants, horses, buffaloes, goats, and cows likewise
always bear flowers [on themselves], it is for the death of their master.

2.3.s:
gṛhe haṃso gṛhe samyaṅmaṇḍūkā jalacāriṇaḥ ..
dvāre praviśya sarpaśca pratimāyāḥ prakalpanam .. 81 ..
2.3.d:
गृहे हंसो गृहे सम्यङ्मण्डूका जलचारिणः ॥
द्वारे प्रविश्य सर्पश्च प्रतिमायाः प्रकल्पनम् ॥ 81 ॥
2.3.m:
A swan in the house, aquatic frogs right in the house,
a snake entering the door, or the fashioning of an image,

2.3.s:
akasmāddhaṭaśabdopi yatra kutrāpi jāyate ..
sravaṃti pramadā yatra bhinnāste syurnavāṃgikāḥ .. 82 ..
2.3.d:
अकस्माद्धटशब्दोपि यत्र कुत्रापि जायते ॥
स्रवंति प्रमदा यत्र भिन्नास्ते स्युर्नवांगिकाः ॥ 82 ॥
2.3.m:
or where the sound of a pot arises suddenly anywhere,
where women discharge [blood], their new limbs being broken,

2.3.s:
gṛhī tatra vinaśyeta saputrapaśubāṃdhavaḥ ..
dhanuḥkhaḍgadharā rātrau madhyāhne cāndrake tathā .. 83 ..
2.3.d:
गृही तत्र विनश्येत सपुत्रपशुबांधवः ॥
धनुःखड्गधरा रात्रौ मध्याह्ने चान्द्रके तथा ॥ 83 ॥
2.3.m:
the householder will perish there along with his sons, cattle, and kin.
At night, or at midday, in the lunar orb, bearing a bow and sword,

2.3.s:
udito dṛśyate vyomni jvalitaḥ pāvakastathā ..
manuṣyāṅganānāṃ maraṇaṃ tathā syādrāṣṭraviplavaḥ .. 84 ..
2.3.d:
उदितो दृश्यते व्योम्नि ज्वलितः पावकस्तथा ॥
मनुष्याङ्गनानां मरणं तथा स्याद्राष्ट्रविप्लवः ॥ 84 ॥
2.3.m:
or a blazing fire is seen risen in the sky,
there will be the death of women, as well as upheaval in the realm.

2.3.s:
rasasiddhāni vastūni surādyāścāpi vā punaḥ ..
hastino madayuktāśca aśvā dhīritahiṃsakāḥ ..
vinaśyaṃti sadā caite śaneradbhutadarśane .. 85 ..
2.3.d:
रससिद्धानि वस्तूनि सुराद्याश्चापि वा पुनः ॥
हस्तिनो मदयुक्ताश्च अश्वा धीरितहिंसकाः ॥
विनश्यंति सदा चैते शनेरद्भुतदर्शने ॥ 85 ॥
2.3.m:
Liquified alchemical substances, or again liquors and such,
elephants in rut, and horses that are reckless and violent,
always perish when there is a portent of Śani.

2.3.s:
nagare vā tathā grāme jāyante tasya vairiṇaḥ ..
divā vā yadi vā rātrau śaneradbhutadarśanam .. 86 ..
2.3.d:
नगरे वा तथा ग्रामे जायन्ते तस्य वैरिणः ॥
दिवा वा यदि वा रात्रौ शनेरद्भुतदर्शनम् ॥ 86 ॥
2.3.m:
Enemies will arise against him in the city or in the village;
by day or by night, it is a portent of Śani.

2.3.s:
mṛgavyāghrādirakṣāṃsi tathā gomahiṣā api ..
utpataṃti yadā caite śaneradbhutamādiśet .. 87 ..
2.3.d:
मृगव्याघ्रादिरक्षांसि तथा गोमहिषा अपि ॥
उत्पतंति यदा चैते शनेरद्भुतमादिशेत् ॥ 87 ॥
2.3.m:
When deer, tigers, and other wild beasts, as well as cattle and buffaloes,
leap up [uncontrollably], one should designate it a portent of Śani.

2.3.s:
nidhimaṃtraṃ pravakṣyāmi yena saṃpadyate śubham ..
juhuyādayutaṃ samyaksasyāṃśca samidhaṃ dvijāḥ .. 88 ..
2.3.d:
निधिमंत्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि येन संपद्यते शुभम् ॥
जुहुयादयुतं सम्यक्सस्यांश्च समिधं द्विजाः ॥ 88 ॥
2.3.m:
I shall declare the treasure-mantra by which good fortune ensues:
O Brahmins, one should properly offer into the fire ten thousand grains and kindling sticks,

2.3.s:
śanno devīti maṃtreṇa śubhārthaṃ śanivāsare ..
caruṃ ca śrapayettatra samuddiśya śanaiścaram .. 89 ..
2.3.d:
शन्नो देवीति मंत्रेण शुभार्थं शनिवासरे ॥
चरुं च श्रपयेत्तत्र समुद्दिश्य शनैश्चरम् ॥ 89 ॥
2.3.m:
with the mantra 'śaṃ no devī' on a Saturday for the sake of auspiciousness;
and there one should cook a caru offering dedicated to Śanaiścara.

2.3.s:
gāṃ ca nīlāṃ tato dadyājjīvadvatsāṃ payasvinīm ..
vāsoyugaṃ ca viprāya suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tathā .. 2.3.20.90 ..
2.3.d:
गां च नीलां ततो दद्याज्जीवद्वत्सां पयस्विनीम् ॥
वासोयुगं च विप्राय सुवर्णं रजतं तथा ॥ 2.3.20.90 ॥
2.3.m:
Then one should give to a Brahmin a dark cow whose calf is living and giving milk,
a pair of garments, gold, and silver.

2.3.s:
dattvā tu śraddhayā samyagdakṣiṇāṃ śirasi sthitām ..
vidhiṃ homāvasāne tu tataḥ saṃpadyate śubham .. 91 ..
2.3.d:
दत्त्वा तु श्रद्धया सम्यग्दक्षिणां शिरसि स्थिताम् ॥
विधिं होमावसाने तु ततः संपद्यते शुभम् ॥ 91 ॥
2.3.m:
Having duly and faithfully presented the sacrificial fee placed on the head,
[and concluded] the rite at the end of the fire offering, good fortune will ensue.

2.3.s:
yadā dvāre godhikā ca śaṃkhinī praviśedgṛham ..
tadā'śubhaṃ vijānīyādrājapīḍā dhanakṣayaḥ ..
ayutaṃ juhuyātsamyaktataḥ saṃpadyate śubham .. 92 ..
2.3.d:
यदा द्वारे गोधिका च शंखिनी प्रविशेद्गृहम् ॥
तदाऽशुभं विजानीयाद्राजपीडा धनक्षयः ॥
अयुतं जुहुयात्सम्यक्ततः संपद्यते शुभम् ॥ 92 ॥
2.3.m:
When an iguana or a śaṅkhinī snake enters the house through the door,
then one should recognise it as inauspicious: torment from the king and loss of wealth.
One should duly offer ten thousand oblations; then good fortune ensues.

2.3.s:
vinā garjitameghena śilāvṛṣṭiḥ prajāyate ..
raktamiśrā hi pāṃḍuśca patantī yatra dṛśyate .. 93 ..
2.3.d:
विना गर्जितमेघेन शिलावृष्टिः प्रजायते ॥
रक्तमिश्रा हि पांडुश्च पतन्ती यत्र दृश्यते ॥ 93 ॥
2.3.m:
A shower of stones occurs without a thundering cloud;
where it is seen falling mixed with blood, or pale,

2.3.s:
tatra saṃdṛśyate cābhraṃ vṛkṣā vātavivarjitāḥ ..
śakradhvajastathā cāpaṃ patanaṃ sumanasya ca .. 94 ..
2.3.d:
तत्र संदृश्यते चाभ्रं वृक्षा वातविवर्जिताः ॥
शक्रध्वजस्तथा चापं पतनं सुमनस्य च ॥ 94 ॥
2.3.m:
and a cloud is seen there, trees devoid of wind [break],
Indra's banner and a bow fall, and the falling of a flower occurs,

2.3.s:
divā śivā purā rauti ulūko vā niśācaraḥ ..
niśi nipatya kākutsthe pradeśe rauti vā vṛṣaḥ .. 95 ..
2.3.d:
दिवा शिवा पुरा रौति उलूको वा निशाचरः ॥
निशि निपत्य काकुत्स्थे प्रदेशे रौति वा वृषः ॥ 95 ॥
2.3.m:
a jackal howls in the city by day, or an owl, the night-prowler [calls],
or an ox howls at night, having collapsed in the area, O descendant of Kakutstha,

2.3.s:
adharmaprabalā deśā rājā dharmaparāṅmukhaḥ ..
anyonyaṃ ca jighāṃsaṃti gobrāhmaṇamathāpi vā .. 96 ..
2.3.d:
अधर्मप्रबला देशा राजा धर्मपराङ्मुखः ॥
अन्योन्यं च जिघांसंति गोब्राह्मणमथापि वा ॥ 96 ॥
2.3.m:
countries will be dominated by unrighteousness, the king will be averse to virtue,
and [men] will seek to kill one another, or a cow or a Brahmin.

2.3.s:
gṛhe gṛhī vinaśyecca saputrapaśubāṃdhavaḥ ..
utsānaṃ dvāradeśe'sya maraṇaṃ rāṣṭravibhramaḥ .. 97 ..
2.3.d:
गृहे गृही विनश्येच्च सपुत्रपशुबांधवः ॥
उत्सानं द्वारदेशेऽस्य मरणं राष्ट्रविभ्रमः ॥ 97 ॥
2.3.m:
In the house, the householder will perish along with his sons, cattle, and kin;
there will be distress at his doorway, death, and confusion in the realm.

2.3.s:
rājyanāśo bhavedrājño maraṇaṃ vāhanasya ca ..
viparītāni deśāni kramataḥ saṃbhavaṃti hi .. 98 ..
2.3.d:
राज्यनाशो भवेद्राज्ञो मरणं वाहनस्य च ॥
विपरीतानि देशानि क्रमतः संभवंति हि ॥ 98 ॥
2.3.m:
There will be the loss of the king's realm and the death of his mount;
calamities will indeed arise successively in the provinces.

2.3.s:
rāhuṇā grastasūryo'pi niśi cātha yadā divā ..
tārakāgaṇavaccaiva rājñāṃ nidhanakārakaḥ .. 99 ..
2.3.d:
राहुणा ग्रस्तसूर्योऽपि निशि चाथ यदा दिवा ॥
तारकागणवच्चैव राज्ञां निधनकारकः ॥ 99 ॥
2.3.m:
When the sun is eclipsed by Rāhu, whether at night or by day,
or resembles a cluster of stars, it brings destruction to kings.

2.3.s:
sahāmātyā vinaśyaṃti svarge ye ca sudurjayāḥ ..
paracakreṇa pātyaṃte rājāno nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 2.3.20.100 ..
2.3.d:
सहामात्या विनश्यंति स्वर्गे ये च सुदुर्जयाः ॥
परचक्रेण पात्यंते राजानो नात्र संशयः ॥ 2.3.20.100 ॥
2.3.m:
Kings perish together with their ministers, even those invincible in heaven;
they are cast down by a hostile army—of this there is no doubt.

2.3.s:
chāyādhvajaśca gagane dṛśyate cetkadācana ..
darśanādeva rājñastu vināśaḥ saharāṣṭrakaiḥ .. 101 ..
2.3.d:
छायाध्वजश्च गगने दृश्यते चेत्कदाचन ॥
दर्शनादेव राज्ञस्तु विनाशः सहराष्ट्रकैः ॥ 101 ॥
2.3.m:
And if ever a shadow-banner is seen in the sky,
by its mere sighting comes the destruction of the king along with his subjects.

2.3.s:
jvalito dṛśyate yatra pāvakaśca sakṛjjale ..
vajre śirasi gātre vā jīvitaṃ tasya durlabham .. 102 ..
2.3.d:
ज्वलितो दृश्यते यत्र पावकश्च सकृज्जले ॥
वज्रे शिरसि गात्रे वा जीवितं तस्य दुर्लभम् ॥ 102 ॥
2.3.m:
Where a blazing fire is seen suddenly in water,
or a thunderbolt strikes the head or body, his life is hard to preserve.

2.3.s:
dvāropāṃte tathā staṃbhe āgnirvā dhūma eva vā ..
puruṣasya tu tatraiva maraṇaṃ jāyate dhruvam .. 103 ..
2.3.d:
द्वारोपांते तथा स्तंभे आग्निर्वा धूम एव वा ॥
पुरुषस्य तु तत्रैव मरणं जायते ध्रुवम् ॥ 103 ॥
2.3.m:
Near the door, or upon a pillar, fire or smoke appears;
the death of the man there will surely occur.

2.3.s:
gagane'śanighātaśca śaktihastena vā punaḥ ..
abdasyābhyaṃtare tasya maraṇaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ..104..
2.3.d:
गगनेऽशनिघातश्च शक्तिहस्तेन वा पुनः ॥
अब्दस्याभ्यंतरे तस्य मरणं नात्र संशयः ॥104॥
2.3.m:
Or again a lightning strike in the sky, or by the hand of a spear-wielder;
within a year his death will occur—there is no doubt of this.

2.3.s:
śikhāvalayamadhye tu sadhūmaḥ pāvakodgamaḥ ..
dṛśyate nagare madhye tatraivādbhutadarśanam .. 105 ..
2.3.d:
शिखावलयमध्ये तु सधूमः पावकोद्गमः ॥
दृश्यते नगरे मध्ये तत्रैवाद्भुतदर्शनम् ॥ 105 ॥
2.3.m: If within the circle of the flame an outbreak of smoky fire is seen / in the middle of a city, that indeed is an portentous sight.

2.3.s:
śavasya nīyamānasya utthānaṃ vā pramādataḥ ..
sthāpitasya ca liṃgasya anyatra gamanaṃ tathā .. 106 ..
2.3.d:
शवस्य नीयमानस्य उत्थानं वा प्रमादतः ॥
स्थापितस्य च लिंगस्य अन्यत्र गमनं तथा ॥ 106 ॥
2.3.m: Or if a corpse being carried away should rise up through error, / and likewise if an installed linga should move elsewhere,

2.3.s:
nirghātaścāpi bhūkaṃpo nivātolkāpradarśanam ..
akāle puṣpitā vṛkṣāḥ phalaṃ cākālasaṃbhavam .. .. 107 ..
2.3.d:
निर्घातश्चापि भूकंपो निवातोल्काप्रदर्शनम् ॥
अकाले पुष्पिता वृक्षाः फलं चाकालसंभवम् ॥ ॥ 107 ॥
2.3.m: a thunderclap [from a cloudless sky], an earthquake, the sight of a meteor falling in windless weather, / trees blossoming out of season, and fruit appearing out of season,

2.3.s:
animittāni sarvāṇi dūramāgatya nirbharam ..
animittasya nāśo yaḥ saiṃhikeyakṛtasya ca .. 108 ..
2.3.d:
अनिमित्तानि सर्वाणि दूरमागत्य निर्भरम् ॥
अनिमित्तस्य नाशो यः सैंहिकेयकृतस्य च ॥ 108 ॥
2.3.m: all these are inauspicious portents having arrived from afar with full force. / For the destruction of the portent caused by the son of Siṃhikā,

2.3.s:
narāṇāmāsanaṃ caiva gavāṃ vā mānuṣīgirā ..
pakṣamātrāṃtare tasya putrasya maraṇaṃ diśet .. 109 ..
2.3.d:
नराणामासनं चैव गवां वा मानुषीगिरा ॥
पक्षमात्रांतरे तस्य पुत्रस्य मरणं दिशेत् ॥ 109 ॥
2.3.m: or if an assembly of men or cattle speaks with a human voice, / one should foretell the death of his son within half a month.

2.3.s:
ayutaṃ juhuyāttatra rāhumuddiśya yatnataḥ ..
śāṃtimatra pravakṣyāmi yayā saṃpadyate śubham .. 2.3.20.110 ..
2.3.d:
अयुतं जुहुयात्तत्र राहुमुद्दिश्य यत्नतः ॥
शांतिमत्र प्रवक्ष्यामि यया संपद्यते शुभम् ॥ 2.3.20.110 ॥
2.3.m: There one should carefully make ten thousand oblations dedicated to Rāhu. / I shall declare the appeasement rite here, by which good fortune is attained.

2.3.s:
dadhimadhughṛtāktaṃ ca kuryāddūrvākṣataṃ tathā ..
kalāyu iti mantreṇa juhuyādravivāsare .. 111 ..
2.3.d:
दधिमधुघृताक्तं च कुर्याद्दूर्वाक्षतं तथा ॥
कलायु इति मन्त्रेण जुहुयाद्रविवासरे ॥ 111 ॥
2.3.m: One should prepare dūrvā grass and unbroken grain smeared with curd, honey, and ghee; / with the mantra 'kalāyu...', one should offer oblations on a Sunday.

2.3.s:
caruṃ ca śrapayettatra rāhumudiśya saṃśrayāt ..
homaṃ kuryāttato gāṃ ca kapilāṃ ca payasvinīm .. 112 ..
2.3.d:
चरुं च श्रपयेत्तत्र राहुमुदिश्य संश्रयात् ॥
होमं कुर्यात्ततो गां च कपिलां च पयस्विनीम् ॥ 112 ॥
2.3.m: And there one should cook a caru offering dedicated to Rāhu as a refuge; / then one should perform the fire offering and give a tawny, milk-giving cow,

2.3.s:
atasī tilaśaṃkhau vā vāsoyugamathāpi vā ..
śraddhayā rāhumuddiśya dadyādviprāya dakṣiṇām .. 113 ..
2.3.d:
अतसी तिलशंखौ वा वासोयुगमथापि वा ॥
श्रद्धया राहुमुद्दिश्य दद्याद्विप्राय दक्षिणाम् ॥ 113 ॥
2.3.m: or flax, sesame, and a conch, or a pair of garments; / with faith, intending it for Rāhu, one should give a priestly gift to a Brahmin.

2.3.s:
duritasya vināśāya tasya saṃpadyate śubham ..
dadhimadhughṛtakṣīreṇa vāruṇena ca vāruṇe .. 114 ..
2.3.d:
दुरितस्य विनाशाय तस्य संपद्यते शुभम् ॥
दधिमधुघृतक्षीरेण वारुणेन च वारुणे ॥ 114 ॥
2.3.m: For the destruction of misfortune, good fortune comes to him; / with curd, honey, ghee, and milk, [offering] to Varuṇa in the Varuṇa direction.

2.3.s:
dṛśyate cādbhutaṃ teṣu viśiṣṭairdoṣadarśibhiḥ ..
gṛhī tatra vinaṣṭaśca bhavetsapaśubāṃdhavaḥ ..115..
2.3.d:
दृश्यते चाद्भुतं तेषु विशिष्टैर्दोषदर्शिभिः ॥
गृही तत्र विनष्टश्च भवेत्सपशुबांधवः ॥115॥
2.3.m: If a portent is seen among these by eminent observers of faults, / the householder there would be ruined along with his cattle and kin.

2.3.s:
dṛśyaṃte tatra krauñcāśca jaṃbukā gṛdhravāyasāḥ ..
dāruṇaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ ghoraṃ nṛtyaṃti ca hasaṃti ca ..1 16..
2.3.d:
दृश्यंते तत्र क्रौञ्चाश्च जंबुका गृध्रवायसाः ॥
दारुणं भीषणं घोरं नृत्यंति च हसंति च ॥1 16॥
2.3.m: If curlews, jackals, vultures, and crows are seen there, / dancing and laughing in a terrible, frightening, and dreadful manner,

2.3.s:
maithunāni ca sarveṣāṃ yasya vāse bhavedyadi ..
mṛtyustasya bhavedāśu īśvarasya ca śāsanāt .. 117 ..
2.3.d:
मैथुनानि च सर्वेषां यस्य वासे भवेद्यदि ॥
मृत्युस्तस्य भवेदाशु ईश्वरस्य च शासनात् ॥ 117 ॥
2.3.m: and if matings of all kinds occur in his dwelling, / death would come to him swiftly by the ordinance of the Lord.

2.3.s:
dhūmaketuryadā vyomni jvalatpāvaka sannibhaḥ ..
sthānātsthānāṃtaraṃ yāti bhūmau vā patate bhṛśam ..
sabaṃdhurasyate rājā paracakraiḥ sa pīḍitaḥ .. 118 ..
2.3.d:
धूमकेतुर्यदा व्योम्नि ज्वलत्पावक सन्निभः ॥
स्थानात्स्थानांतरं याति भूमौ वा पतते भृशम् ॥
सबंधुरस्यते राजा परचक्रैः स पीडितः ॥ 118 ॥
2.3.m: When a comet resembling blazing fire moves from place to place in the sky, / or violently falls to the earth, / the king, afflicted by foreign armies, is destroyed along with his kinsmen.

2.3.s:
durbhikṣaṃ maraṇaṃ caiva ciraṃ rāṣṭre bhaviṣyati ..
gāvo markaṭakuṃbhā va viśaṃte gṛhaveśmani .. 119 ..
2.3.d:
दुर्भिक्षं मरणं चैव चिरं राष्ट्रे भविष्यति ॥
गावो मर्कटकुंभा व विशंते गृहवेश्मनि ॥ 119 ॥
2.3.m: Famine and death will endure for a long time in the realm. / If cows, monkeys, or water-jars enter into the dwelling of a house,

2.3.s:
gāvaśca tasya naśyaṃti dārāpatyadhanāni ca ..
anyasya doṣo bhavati gṛhe yāṃti pramādataḥ .. 2.3.20.120 ..
2.3.d:
गावश्च तस्य नश्यंति दारापत्यधनानि च ॥
अन्यस्य दोषो भवति गृहे यांति प्रमादतः ॥ 2.3.20.120 ॥
2.3.m: his cows perish, as well as his wife, offspring, and wealth. / It brings misfortune to another if they enter a house by mistake.

2.3.s:
abdāṃtare bhavenmṛtyurvirajā hi bhaviṣyati ..
śāṃtimatra pravakṣyāmi yayā saṃpadyate śubham .. 121 ..
2.3.d:
अब्दांतरे भवेन्मृत्युर्विरजा हि भविष्यति ॥
शांतिमत्र प्रवक्ष्यामि यया संपद्यते शुभम् ॥ 121 ॥
2.3.m: Death will occur within a year; indeed, he will become free of dust [i.e., dead]. / I shall declare the appeasement rite here, by which good fortune is attained.

2.3.s:
saptāśvarathasaṃyuktaṃ hemacchatravibhūṣitam ..
viprāya maṃḍapaṃ dadyādbilvapatramathāpi vā .. 122 ..
2.3.d:
सप्ताश्वरथसंयुक्तं हेमच्छत्रविभूषितम् ॥
विप्राय मंडपं दद्याद्बिल्वपत्रमथापि वा ॥ 122 ॥
2.3.m: One should give to a Brahmin a pavilion equipped with a seven-horse chariot / and adorned with a royal parasol of gold, or else a bilva leaf.

2.3.s:
aiṃdreṇaiva tu mantreṇa homaḥ kāryo dvijātibhiḥ ..
akasmācchālatālākṣakhadirotpalaserakāḥ .. 123 ..
2.3.d:
ऐंद्रेणैव तु मन्त्रेण होमः कार्यो द्विजातिभिः ॥
अकस्माच्छालतालाक्षखदिरोत्पलसेरकाः ॥ 123 ॥
2.3.m: The twice-born should perform the fire offering with the mantra addressed to Indra. / If suddenly sāla, palm, akṣa, khadira, blue lotus, or seraka plants

2.3.s:
gṛhamadhye prajāyeta ketoradbhutadarśanam ..
haṃso vā droṇakāko vā mayūro vā gṛhopari .. 124 ..
2.3.d:
गृहमध्ये प्रजायेत केतोरद्भुतदर्शनम् ॥
हंसो वा द्रोणकाको वा मयूरो वा गृहोपरि ॥ 124 ॥
2.3.m: If [these] should grow inside the house, it is an portentous sight of Ketu; / or if a swan, a raven, or a peacock is seen above the house,

2.3.s:
gṛhe tasya mahotpātaḥ ketoradbhutadarśanam ..
śāṃtimatra pravakṣyāmi yayā saṃpadyate śubham..125..
2.3.d:
गृहे तस्य महोत्पातः केतोरद्भुतदर्शनम् ॥
शांतिमत्र प्रवक्ष्यामि यया संपद्यते शुभम्॥125॥
2.3.m: a great calamity occurs in his house: it is an portentous sight of Ketu. / I shall declare the appeasement rite here, by which good fortune is attained.

2.3.s:
dadhimadhughṛtāktaṃ ca juhuyādayutaṃ kuśam..
tryaṃbakaṃ ceti mantreṇa ketavebhivape ccarum .. 126 ..
2.3.d:
दधिमधुघृताक्तं च जुहुयादयुतं कुशम्॥
त्र्यंबकं चेति मन्त्रेण केतवेभिवपे च्चरुम् ॥ 126 ॥
2.3.m: One should offer ten thousand kuśa blades smeared with curd, honey, and ghee; / and with the mantra 'Tryambaka...', one should scatter the caru offering for Ketu.

2.3.s:
nīlāṃ dhenuṃ savatsāṃ ca bahukṣīrapradāṃ tathā ..
mṛttikāṃ hemavāsaśca nānālaṃkārameva ca .. 127 ..
2.3.d:
नीलां धेनुं सवत्सां च बहुक्षीरप्रदां तथा ॥
मृत्तिकां हेमवासश्च नानालंकारमेव च ॥ 127 ॥
2.3.m: A dark cow together with her calf, providing abundant milk, / earth, gold, garments, and various ornaments [should be given].

2.3.s:
dakṣiṇāṃ ca pravakṣyāmi yasya nāsti pratikriyā ..
devamuddiśya dānena homena caruṇā tathā .. 128 ..
2.3.d:
दक्षिणां च प्रवक्ष्यामि यस्य नास्ति प्रतिक्रिया ॥
देवमुद्दिश्य दानेन होमेन चरुणा तथा ॥ 128 ॥
2.3.m: I shall declare the priestly gift where there is no other remedy: / by gifting, by fire offering, and likewise by caru dedicated to the deity.

2.3.s:
dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi cchāyāṃ yaḥ paśyedātmanaḥ svayam ..
svacchāyāṃ pādukasyaiva paśyetpañcaśirodvayam .. 129 ..
2.3.d:
दक्षिणस्यां दिशि च्छायां यः पश्येदात्मनः स्वयम् ॥
स्वच्छायां पादुकस्यैव पश्येत्पञ्चशिरोद्वयम् ॥ 129 ॥
2.3.m: One who personally sees his own shadow in the southern quarter, / or sees the shadow of his shoe, or sees five or two heads,

2.3.s:
evamevaiva yacchinnaṃ śinaṣṭi ca tato hitam ..
śīghraṃ nāśamavāpnoti saptāhānnātra saṃśayaḥ .. 2.3.20.130 ..
2.3.d:
एवमेवैव यच्छिन्नं शिनष्टि च ततो हितम् ॥
शीघ्रं नाशमवाप्नोति सप्ताहान्नात्र संशयः ॥ 2.3.20.130 ॥
2.3.m: or sees it severed in that very manner, what good remains for him then? / He swiftly attains destruction within seven days; there is no doubt here.

2.3.s:
uccāvacānpravakṣyāmi yathā śāstreṇa coditam ..
kākamārjāraśūkānāṃ kapotānāṃ viśeṣataḥ ..
maithunaṃ dṛśyate yatra tacca rāhormahādbhutam .. 131 ..
2.3.d:
उच्चावचान्प्रवक्ष्यामि यथा शास्त्रेण चोदितम् ॥
काकमार्जारशूकानां कपोतानां विशेषतः ॥
मैथुनं दृश्यते यत्र तच्च राहोर्महाद्भुतम् ॥ 131 ॥
2.3.m: I shall declare diverse portents, as enjoined by the scripture: / where copulation of crows, cats, porcupines, and especially pigeons / is seen, that is a great portent of Rāhu.

2.3.s:
śanimuddiśya juhuyādayutaṃ śanivāsare ..
pūjayedarkapuṣpeṇa śatena juhuyāccarum .. 132 ..
2.3.d:
शनिमुद्दिश्य जुहुयादयुतं शनिवासरे ॥
पूजयेदर्कपुष्पेण शतेन जुहुयाच्चरुम् ॥ 132 ॥
2.3.m: One should offer ten thousand oblations dedicated to Saturn on a Saturday; / one should worship with arka flowers, and offer a caru with a hundred [oblations].

2.3.s:
kṛtvā tatraiva paśyeta śaneradbhutadarśanam ..
aṣṭāviṃśaṃ caruṃ kṛtvā tataḥ śāṃtirbhaveddhruvam 133 ..
2.3.d:
कृत्वा तत्रैव पश्येत शनेरद्भुतदर्शनम् ॥
अष्टाविंशं चरुं कृत्वा ततः शांतिर्भवेद्ध्रुवम् 133 ॥
2.3.m: Having done this right there, one should examine the portentous sight of Saturn; / having prepared twenty-eight caru offerings, appeasement will certainly ensue.

2.3.s:
bhujapadostathā cakṣuḥspaṃdane maraṇaṃ diśet ..
tattu somādbhutaṃ vidyādvāmadakṣiṇataḥ kramāt .. 134 ..
2.3.d:
भुजपदोस्तथा चक्षुःस्पंदने मरणं दिशेत् ॥
तत्तु सोमाद्भुतं विद्याद्वामदक्षिणतः क्रमात् ॥ 134 ॥
2.3.m: If there is twitching in the arms, feet, or eyes, one should foretell death; / one should know that to be a lunar portent, on the left and right respectively.

2.3.s:
kṛṣṇapakṣe bhavedvāme viparīte'dbhutaṃ diśet ..
aniṣṭasūcakaṃ yasmāttasmācchāṃtiṃ prakalpayet..135..
2.3.d:
कृष्णपक्षे भवेद्वामे विपरीतेऽद्भुतं दिशेत् ॥
अनिष्टसूचकं यस्मात्तस्माच्छांतिं प्रकल्पयेत्॥135॥
2.3.m: In the dark fortnight, it is [ominous] on the left; one should declare it an ominous portent if contrary. / Because it indicates misfortune, one should therefore perform an appeasement rite.

2.3.s:
śatārddhaṃ ravimuddiśya śāntyarthe homamācaret ..
carupākavidhānena yavaistilasusarpiṣā .. 136 ..
2.3.d:
शतार्द्धं रविमुद्दिश्य शान्त्यर्थे होममाचरेत् ॥
चरुपाकविधानेन यवैस्तिलसुसर्पिषा ॥ 136 ॥
2.3.m: One should perform a fire offering of fifty oblations dedicated to the Sun for appeasement, / following the procedure for cooking caru, with barley, sesame, and fine ghee.

2.3.s:
pustake yajñasūtraṃ ca asatpātre carau tu vā ..
śakravastrapradagdhe ca sūryasyādbhutadarśanam .. 137 ..
2.3.d:
पुस्तके यज्ञसूत्रं च असत्पात्रे चरौ तु वा ॥
शक्रवस्त्रप्रदग्धे च सूर्यस्याद्भुतदर्शनम् ॥ 137 ॥
2.3.m: If a sacred thread is on a book, or on an unworthy vessel, or on the caru, / or if Indra's cloth is burned, it is an portentous sight of the Sun.

2.3.s:
hayamāraṃ trimadhvaktaṃ juhuyādiṣṭasiddhaye ..
devapustakaratnāni maṇikāṃcanameva ca .. 138 ..
2.3.d:
हयमारं त्रिमध्वक्तं जुहुयादिष्टसिद्धये ॥
देवपुस्तकरत्नानि मणिकांचनमेव च ॥ 138 ॥
2.3.m: One should offer oleander smeared with the three sweets for the attainment of one's desires; / [if portents occur regarding] images of gods, books, jewels, gems, and gold,

2.3.s:
lohitasyādbhutaṃ vidyātsahasraṃ ca viśodhanam ..
devāgāre tathā godhā śaṃkhinī praviśetkvacit .. 139 ..
2.3.d:
लोहितस्याद्भुतं विद्यात्सहस्रं च विशोधनम् ॥
देवागारे तथा गोधा शंखिनी प्रविशेत्क्वचित् ॥ 139 ॥
2.3.m: one should know it as an portent of Mars, and a thousand [oblations] is the purification. / If an iguana or a conch-snail enters a temple of the gods anywhere,

2.3.s:
droṇakāko bakaścaiva ulūkadvayameva ca ..
raktakaṃṭhaḥ kapotaśca vyāghra eṇaśca vā viśet .. 2.3.20.140 ..
2.3.d:
द्रोणकाको बकश्चैव उलूकद्वयमेव च ॥
रक्तकंठः कपोतश्च व्याघ्र एणश्च वा विशेत् ॥ 2.3.20.140 ॥
2.3.m: or if a raven, a crane, or a pair of owls, / or a red-throated pigeon, a tiger, or a blackbuck enters,

2.3.s:
yasya devagṛhaṃ paśyettasya tasyāyutaṃ hunet ..
na cātra gṛhavaikṛtyaṃ hasanaṃ yadi dṛśyate ..
saṃpattisūcakaṃ gehe maraṇaṃ duḥkhadarśanam .. 141 ..
2.3.d:
यस्य देवगृहं पश्येत्तस्य तस्यायुतं हुनेत् ॥
न चात्र गृहवैकृत्यं हसनं यदि दृश्यते ॥
संपत्तिसूचकं गेहे मरणं दुःखदर्शनम् ॥ 141 ॥
2.3.m: in whatever house of a deity one sees this, one should offer ten thousand oblations for it. / Nor is there any deformity in the house here; if laughing is seen,

2.3.s:
kraṃdane hatarājyena gajāśvavāhane kvacit ..
sūryamuddiśya juhuyādayutaṃ sarvasiddhaye .. 142 ..
2.3.d:
क्रंदने हतराज्येन गजाश्ववाहने क्वचित् ॥
सूर्यमुद्दिश्य जुहुयादयुतं सर्वसिद्धये ॥ 142 ॥
2.3.m: it indicates wealth in the house, [whereas] death and misery are seen / in weeping; if the kingdom is ruined, or anywhere on an elephant or horse mount, / one should offer ten thousand oblations dedicated to the Sun for complete success.

2.3.s:
pramādātkaṃpane hāniḥ svede jāte vipadbhavet ..
kṣīrasrāve ca rudhire tatra rājye mahadbhayam .. 143 ..
2.3.d:
प्रमादात्कंपने हानिः स्वेदे जाते विपद्भवेत् ॥
क्षीरस्रावे च रुधिरे तत्र राज्ये महद्भयम् ॥ 143 ॥
2.3.m: From trembling due to an accident there is loss; when sweating occurs, there is misfortune; / and if milk or blood flows, there is great terror in that kingdom.

2.3.s:
gocchāgau vātha gomāyurgṛhopari pranṛtyati ..
yadā rauti divā pherustadā nāśo bhaveddhruvam .. 144 ..
2.3.d:
गोच्छागौ वाथ गोमायुर्गृहोपरि प्रनृत्यति ॥
यदा रौति दिवा फेरुस्तदा नाशो भवेद्ध्रुवम् ॥ 144 ॥
2.3.m: If a cow, a goat, or a jackal dances upon a house, / [or] when a jackal howls by day, then destruction will surely follow.

2.3.s:
śvajaṃbukāvatha vyāghro yathāśakti ca dhāvati ..
īśāne mahiṣastadvattadā deśe ca viplavaḥ .. 145 ..
2.3.d:
श्वजंबुकावथ व्याघ्रो यथाशक्ति च धावति ॥
ईशाने महिषस्तद्वत्तदा देशे च विप्लवः ॥ 145 ॥
2.3.m: If a dog and a jackal, or a tiger runs with all its might, / or likewise a buffalo in the northeast, then there will be upheaval in the land.

2.3.s:
rāhoradbhutamudiśya sahasraṃ juhuyāccarum ..
vṛkṣādbhutaṃ yadā paśyettatra tasyāṃ parityajet ..
yadgṛheṣu hutaṃ yāti deśaviplavamādiśet .. .. 146 ..
2.3.d:
राहोरद्भुतमुदिश्य सहस्रं जुहुयाच्चरुम् ॥
वृक्षाद्भुतं यदा पश्येत्तत्र तस्यां परित्यजेत् ॥
यद्गृहेषु हुतं याति देशविप्लवमादिशेत् ॥ ॥ 146 ॥
2.3.m: Intending it for an portent of Rāhu, one should offer a thousand oblations of caru. / When one sees a portent involving trees, one should abandon it in that [direction]; / if what is offered goes into houses, one should predict upheaval in the land.

2.3.s:
deśe vā nagare grāme āraṇyapaśubandhanam ..
sarpe vā viparītaṃ ca māṃsapiṃḍamathāpi vā ..
tadgṛhe maraṇaṃ caiva deśa viplavamādiśet .. 147 ..
2.3.d:
देशे वा नगरे ग्रामे आरण्यपशुबन्धनम् ॥
सर्पे वा विपरीतं च मांसपिंडमथापि वा ॥
तद्गृहे मरणं चैव देश विप्लवमादिशेत् ॥ 147 ॥
2.3.m: If in a country, city, or village a wild animal is bound, / or if a snake [gives birth to] an unnatural form or a lump of flesh, / death [occurs] in that house and one should foretell catastrophe for the realm.

2.3.s:
divādbhute'yutaṃ rātrau dviguṇaṃ ca bhaveddhruvam ..
dviguṇaṃ cāpi saṃdhyāyāmardharātre caturguṇam .. 148 ..
2.3.d:
दिवाद्भुतेऽयुतं रात्रौ द्विगुणं च भवेद्ध्रुवम् ॥
द्विगुणं चापि संध्यायामर्धरात्रे चतुर्गुणम् ॥ 148 ॥
2.3.m: In the case of a daytime portent, ten thousand [oblations should be offered], and at night it certainly must be doubled; / at twilight it is also doubled, and at midnight it is quadrupled.

2.3.s:
akāle tatra maraṇamakāle gṛhiṇīmṛtiḥ ..
saurādbhutaṃ vijānīyādaśubhe vā viśodhanam .. 149 ..
2.3.d:
अकाले तत्र मरणमकाले गृहिणीमृतिः ॥
सौराद्भुतं विजानीयादशुभे वा विशोधनम् ॥ 149 ॥
2.3.m: Untimely death [occurs] there, [and] untimely death of the housewife. / One should recognise it as a solar portent, or [perform] purification in the event of inauspiciousness.

2.3.s:
ekaikasyāyutaṃ yatra kuryāttatraiva homayet ..
sāṃgopāṃgena sahita maṣṭāvaṣṭau hutaṃ ca vā .. 2.3.20.150 ..
2.3.d:
एकैकस्यायुतं यत्र कुर्यात्तत्रैव होमयेत् ॥
सांगोपांगेन सहित मष्टावष्टौ हुतं च वा ॥ 2.3.20.150 ॥
2.3.m: Where one should offer ten thousand for each one, there one should make the oblation; / together with all the principal and subsidiary limbs, or an oblation of eight each.

2.3.s:
adhipratyadhisahitaṃ gṛhapakṣe'pi sattamāḥ ..
tanmānena hutaṃ viprā kuryāttatraiva bhūṣaṇam .. 151 ..
2.3.d:
अधिप्रत्यधिसहितं गृहपक्षेऽपि सत्तमाः ॥
तन्मानेन हुतं विप्रा कुर्यात्तत्रैव भूषणम् ॥ 151 ॥
2.3.m: Together with the presiding and secondary deities, and also on the side of the planets, O best of men; / according to that measure, O brāhmaṇas, one should make the oblation, and right there perform the adornment.

2.3.s:
ekaikasyāhutaṃ viprā aṣṭāvaṣṭau hutaṃ ca vā ..
adhipratyadhidevānāṃ yāścānyāścāṃgadevatāḥ .. 152 ..
2.3.d:
एकैकस्याहुतं विप्रा अष्टावष्टौ हुतं च वा ॥
अधिप्रत्यधिदेवानां याश्चान्याश्चांगदेवताः ॥ 152 ॥
2.3.m: An oblation for each, O brāhmaṇas, or an oblation of eight each, / for the presiding and secondary deities, and whichever other subordinate deities there are.

2.3.s:
mānāṃtaṃ ca dadetpūrṇāṃ dattvā pūrṇāṃ na homayet ..
vakṣye grahamakhe mānaṃ yena mānena sidhyati .. 153 ..
2.3.d:
मानांतं च ददेत्पूर्णां दत्त्वा पूर्णां न होमयेत् ॥
वक्ष्ये ग्रहमखे मानं येन मानेन सिध्यति ॥ 153 ॥
2.3.m: At the end of the measure one should offer the full oblation; having offered the full oblation, one should not sacrifice further. / I shall explain the measure in the planetary sacrifice, by which measure it succeeds.

2.3.s:
amānakaraṇe doṣastasmānmānaṃ na hāpayet ..
paṃkticatvāriṃśadādyaiścaturdhā vibhajennaraḥ .. 154..
2.3.d:
अमानकरणे दोषस्तस्मान्मानं न हापयेत् ॥
पंक्तिचत्वारिंशदाद्यैश्चतुर्धा विभजेन्नरः ॥ 154॥
2.3.m: In omitting the measure there is a fault; therefore one should not diminish the measure. / A man should divide [the oblations] into four parts, beginning with rows of forty.

2.3.s:
aniṣṭāya tato dadyāccaruhomaṃ vibhāgaśaḥ ..
adhipratyadhidevānāmaṣṭāvaṣṭa hyudāhṛtam ..155 ..
2.3.d:
अनिष्टाय ततो दद्याच्चरुहोमं विभागशः ॥
अधिप्रत्यधिदेवानामष्टावष्ट ह्युदाहृतम् ॥155 ॥
2.3.m: Then one should offer the oblation of boiled-rice offering portion by portion for the afflicted [planet]. / For the presiding and secondary deities, eight each is declared.

2.3.s:
tryaṃbakādiṣu maṃtreṣu homatrayamudāhṛtam ..
dhanaṃjaye tathā dadyāccaruhomaṃ vibhāgataḥ .. 156 ..
2.3.d:
त्र्यंबकादिषु मंत्रेषु होमत्रयमुदाहृतम् ॥
धनंजये तथा दद्याच्चरुहोमं विभागतः ॥ 156 ॥
2.3.m: Three oblations are declared for the mantras beginning with Tryambaka. / Likewise, one should offer the oblation of boiled-rice offering portion by portion to Dhanañjaya.

2.3.s:
ādityāyāṣṭāvaṣṭāvadhikakalpayetsudhīḥ ..
śatahome tu sarvatra daśāṃgaṃ kalpayennaraḥ .. 157 ..
2.3.d:
आदित्यायाष्टावष्टावधिककल्पयेत्सुधीः ॥
शतहोमे तु सर्वत्र दशांगं कल्पयेन्नरः ॥ 157 ॥
2.3.m: A wise man should assign an excess of eight each to the Sun. / But in a hundred-oblation sacrifice everywhere, a man should assign ten parts.

2.3.s:
aniṣṭāya yugāṃgaṃ tu grahebhyo hyaṃganāya ca ..
adhipratyadhidevānāṃ tathaivāṃgaṃ prakalpayet .. 158 ..
2.3.d:
अनिष्टाय युगांगं तु ग्रहेभ्यो ह्यंगनाय च ॥
अधिप्रत्यधिदेवानां तथैवांगं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 158 ॥
2.3.m: Four parts for the afflicted [planet], and parts for the planets and the chief [deity]; / likewise one should assign parts for the presiding and secondary deities.

2.3.s:
dvau tu dadyāttryaṃbakāya tathā dhanaṃjayāya ca ..
tatra homo nāyakāya sarvatraiva vicakṣaṇaḥ .. 159 ..
2.3.d:
द्वौ तु दद्यात्त्र्यंबकाय तथा धनंजयाय च ॥
तत्र होमो नायकाय सर्वत्रैव विचक्षणः ॥ 159 ॥
2.3.m: One should offer two to Tryambaka and likewise to Dhanañjaya. / In that rite, the discerning person always makes an oblation for the chief deity.

2.3.s:
sahasre caiva viṃśāṃge aniṣṭāya daśāṃśakam ..
pañcāṃśena grahāṇāṃ ca pañcāṃśena yavānapi .. 2.3.20.160 ..
2.3.d:
सहस्रे चैव विंशांगे अनिष्टाय दशांशकम् ॥
पञ्चांशेन ग्रहाणां च पञ्चांशेन यवानपि ॥ 2.3.20.160 ॥
2.3.m: And in a thousand [oblations], with twenty parts, one-tenth part is for the afflicted [planet], / five parts are for the planets, and five parts of barley grains.

2.3.s:
tatrāniṣṭe paṃcaśataṃ tasyārdhaṃ grahavāgyataḥ ..
ekatriṃśadbhavenmānam ( 31) anyeṣāṃ tu caturdaśa (14) ..161..
2.3.d:
तत्रानिष्टे पंचशतं तस्यार्धं ग्रहवाग्यतः ॥
एकत्रिंशद्भवेन्मानम् ( 31) अन्येषां तु चतुर्दश (14) ॥161॥
2.3.m: In that case, five hundred [oblations] are for the afflicted [planet]; restrained in speech, half of that is for the planets; / thirty-one is the measure, and for the others, fourteen.

2.3.s:
grahādhikaṃ homayugaṃ tatra bhāge prakalpayet ..
adhātaye ca tithyaṃgaṃ pañcāṃgaṃ yasya cādbhutam .. 162 ..
2.3.d:
ग्रहाधिकं होमयुगं तत्र भागे प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
अधातये च तिथ्यंगं पञ्चांगं यस्य चाद्भुतम् ॥ 162 ॥
2.3.m: In that division one should assign two oblations in excess of the planet; / and for [countering] non-destruction, fifteen parts, and five parts for the one whose portent it is.

2.3.s:
grahebhyaścaiva paṃcāṃgaṃ tatra vāṃgaṃ parānapi ..
ekaikāṃge bhavenmānaṃ ṣaṭśataṃ ṣaṣṭireva ca .. 163 ..
2.3.d:
ग्रहेभ्यश्चैव पंचांगं तत्र वांगं परानपि ॥
एकैकांगे भवेन्मानं षट्शतं षष्टिरेव च ॥ 163 ॥
2.3.m: And five parts for the planets, or parts for the others there. / In each single part the measure would be six hundred and sixty.

2.3.s:
adhikaṃ ca bhavetṣaṣṭirdaśame bhāgaśeṣataḥ ..
aniṣṭāṃśe trisahasraṃ triśataṃ triṃśataṃ tathā .. 164 ..
2.3.d:
अधिकं च भवेत्षष्टिर्दशमे भागशेषतः ॥
अनिष्टांशे त्रिसहस्रं त्रिशतं त्रिंशतं तथा ॥ 164 ॥
2.3.m: And there would be an excess of sixty from the remainder of the tenth division. / In the portion for the afflicted [planet], three thousand, three hundred and thirty.

2.3.s:
catuḥśataṃ grahāṇāṃ ca tathā saptaśatādhikam ..
upagrahebhyo dadyācca paṃcāśītyadhikaṃ śatam .. 165 ..
2.3.d:
चतुःशतं ग्रहाणां च तथा सप्तशताधिकम् ॥
उपग्रहेभ्यो दद्याच्च पंचाशीत्यधिकं शतम् ॥ 165 ॥
2.3.m: Four hundred for the planets, and also an excess of seven hundred. / One should give one hundred and eighty-five to the minor planets.

2.3.s:
tithyaṃgabhāgaḥ śeṣeṇa grahe saptaśatādhikam ..
ekaikaṃ tu grahasyaivamādityāya yugaṃ bhavet .. 166 ..
2.3.d:
तिथ्यंगभागः शेषेण ग्रहे सप्तशताधिकम् ॥
एकैकं तु ग्रहस्यैवमादित्याय युगं भवेत् ॥ 166 ॥
2.3.m: The portion of fifteen parts from the remainder is with an excess of seven hundred for the planet; / thus one for each planet, and there should be four for the Sun.

2.3.s:
grahāṃge yaḥ sthito bhāgo yugalaṃ bhāgaśeṣataḥ ..
tryaṃbakāya ca taddadyāttathā dhanaṃjayāya ca ..167..
2.3.d:
ग्रहांगे यः स्थितो भागो युगलं भागशेषतः ॥
त्र्यंबकाय च तद्दद्यात्तथा धनंजयाय च ॥167॥
2.3.m: The portion situated in the planetary division is a pair from the remainder of the portion; / one should give that to Tryambaka, and likewise to Dhanañjaya.

2.3.s:
śāṃtike pauṣṭike kāmye yadīcchetsukhamātmanaḥ..
grahāṇāṃ cāyutaṃ homaṃ tryahasādhyena homayet .. 168 ..
2.3.d:
शांतिके पौष्टिके काम्ये यदीच्छेत्सुखमात्मनः॥
ग्रहाणां चायुतं होमं त्र्यहसाध्येन होमयेत् ॥ 168 ॥
2.3.m: In pacification rites, prosperity rites, and desire-fulfilling rites, if one desires one's own happiness, / one should offer ten thousand oblations to the planets, accomplished in three days.

2.3.s:
tryahasādhye vidhānaṃ yatpuraivodīritaṃ dvijāḥ ..
idānīṃ prakrameṇaiva yo bhāgaḥ sa nigadyate .. 169 ..
2.3.d:
त्र्यहसाध्ये विधानं यत्पुरैवोदीरितं द्विजाः ॥
इदानीं प्रक्रमेणैव यो भागः स निगद्यते ॥ 169 ॥
2.3.m: The rule concerning what is accomplished in three days has already been stated, O twice-born ones; / now the division according to regular order is described.

2.3.s:
pūrvasmindivase'niṣṭe sahasraṃ triśatottaram ( 1300) ..
itareṣāṃ grahāṇāṃ ca pratyekaṃ tu śataṃ śatam( 100) .. 2.3.20.170 ..
2.3.d:
पूर्वस्मिन्दिवसेऽनिष्टे सहस्रं त्रिशतोत्तरम् ( 1300) ॥
इतरेषां ग्रहाणां च प्रत्येकं तु शतं शतम्( 100) ॥ 2.3.20.170 ॥
2.3.m: On the first day, one thousand and three hundred [oblations] for the afflicted [planet], / and one hundred each for the other planets.

2.3.s:
adhipratyadhidevānāṃ paṃcāśaddhoma ucyate ..
prathamehni pradadyācca militvā trisahasrakam( 3000) .. 171 ..
2.3.d:
अधिप्रत्यधिदेवानां पंचाशद्धोम उच्यते ॥
प्रथमेह्नि प्रदद्याच्च मिलित्वा त्रिसहस्रकम्( 3000) ॥ 171 ॥
2.3.m: Fifty oblations are prescribed for the presiding and secondary deities. / On the first day, combined together, one should offer three thousand.

2.3.s:
dvitīyadivase'niṣṭe dvisahasramudāhṛtam ( 2000) ..
prati grahebhyastriśataṃ dadyādaṣṭa śatādhikam( 108) .. 172 ..
2.3.d:
द्वितीयदिवसेऽनिष्टे द्विसहस्रमुदाहृतम् ( 2000) ॥
प्रति ग्रहेभ्यस्त्रिशतं दद्यादष्ट शताधिकम्( 108) ॥ 172 ॥
2.3.m: On the second day, two thousand [oblations] are prescribed for the afflicted [planet]. / For each of the planets one should offer one hundred and eight.

2.3.s:
upagrahebhyo dadyācca ṣoḍaśabhyo yathākramam ..
ekāśītiṃ dadau yatnādaśītiṃ cāṃtyayordvayoḥ .. 173 ..
2.3.d:
उपग्रहेभ्यो दद्याच्च षोडशभ्यो यथाक्रमम् ॥
एकाशीतिं ददौ यत्नादशीतिं चांत्ययोर्द्वयोः ॥ 173 ॥
2.3.m: And one should offer to the sixteen minor planets in proper order; / he carefully gave eighty-one, and eighty to the last two.

2.3.s:
evaṃ dvitīyadivase militvā ṣaṭsahasrakam ( 6000) ..
aniṣṭāya triśataṃ tu tṛtīyadivase matam..174..
2.3.d:
एवं द्वितीयदिवसे मिलित्वा षट्सहस्रकम् ( 6000) ॥
अनिष्टाय त्रिशतं तु तृतीयदिवसे मतम्॥174॥
2.3.m: Thus, combined together on the second day, six thousand [oblations]. / On the third day, three hundred are prescribed for the afflicted [planet].

2.3.s:
tatpratyekaṃ grahāṇāṃ ca dvācatvāriṃśaducyate ..
adhipratyadhidevānāṃ pratyekaṃ paṃcatriṃśakam .. 175 ..
2.3.d:
तत्प्रत्येकं ग्रहाणां च द्वाचत्वारिंशदुच्यते ॥
अधिप्रत्यधिदेवानां प्रत्येकं पंचत्रिंशकम् ॥ 175 ॥
2.3.m: For each of those planets, forty-two is declared; / for each of the presiding and secondary deities, thirty-five.

2.3.s:
tṛtīyadivase dadyānmilitvaikasahasrakam ( 1000) ..
ādityāya yugaṃ dadyādekaṃ tu tryaṃbakāya ca .. 176 ..
2.3.d:
तृतीयदिवसे दद्यान्मिलित्वैकसहस्रकम् ( 1000) ॥
आदित्याय युगं दद्यादेकं तु त्र्यंबकाय च ॥ 176 ॥
2.3.m: On the third day, combined together, one should offer one thousand. / One should give four to the Sun, and one to Tryambaka.

2.3.s:
dhanaṃjayāya homaikamekaṃ cāyutamucyate ..
tadardhakaṃ grahebhyaśca itarebhyastadardhakam .. 177 ..
2.3.d:
धनंजयाय होमैकमेकं चायुतमुच्यते ॥
तदर्धकं ग्रहेभ्यश्च इतरेभ्यस्तदर्धकम् ॥ 177 ॥
2.3.m: One oblation is declared for Dhanañjaya, and one [share of] ten thousand [is prescribed]. / Half of that is for the planets, and half of that for the others.

2.3.s:
grahāṇāṃ trisahasraṃ tu paṃcānāṃ ca sahasrakam ..
trisahasrabhāgaśeṣamādityāya sahasrakam .. 178 ..
2.3.d:
ग्रहाणां त्रिसहस्रं तु पंचानां च सहस्रकम् ॥
त्रिसहस्रभागशेषमादित्याय सहस्रकम् ॥ 178 ॥
2.3.m: Three thousand for the planets, and one thousand for the five. / From the remainder of the three-thousand share, one thousand is for the Sun.

2.3.s:
tryaṃbakāya tathā dadyāttathā dhanaṃjayāya ca ..
ṣaṭpādādhika ṣaṭaṣaṭkasahasraparisaṃkhyayā ..
navaślokaśatodbhūtaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ syādbhaviṣyakam .. 179 .. ..
..śrīveṅkaṭeśvarārpaṇamastu ..
viṣayānukramaṇikā
2.3.d:
त्र्यंबकाय तथा दद्यात्तथा धनंजयाय च ॥
षट्पादाधिक षटषट्कसहस्रपरिसंख्यया ॥
नवश्लोकशतोद्भूतं संपूर्णं स्याद्भविष्यकम् ॥ 179 ॥ ॥
॥श्रीवेङ्कटेश्वरार्पणमस्तु ॥
विषयानुक्रमणिका
2.3.m:
Likewise one should offer to Tryambaka, and likewise to Dhanañjaya. / By the count of six thousand six hundred and six, plus six quarter-verses, / born of nine hundred verses, the Bhaviṣya [Purāṇa's Madhyamaparvan] is complete.
May this be dedicated to glorious Veṅkaṭeśvara.
